GOPHER DIG - a RetroStone VC game for Windows
(c) 2026 Pierre-Louis Boyer (8BCraft). Code MIT, art/music/sound CC BY-NC-SA 4.0: see LICENSE-gopherdig.txt.

A gopher in a little yellow hard hat drills straight down a well of bright,
jelly-soft blocks. Blocks of one colour stick together: drill one and its
whole group pops. Dig out what holds a group up and it wobbles, then comes
tumbling down: get out from under it, because one block on the head ends the
run. Four of a colour meeting after a fall pop by themselves. Watch the air:
grab the air bubbles buried in the soil, and think twice before drilling
through a hard rock (5 drills, and it costs air). Every 100 m a new stratum,
a little faster: garden soil, red clay, a crystal cave, warm rocks, fossil
beds, a gem core. Your score is how deep you dug. Medals at 60, 200, 400 and
600 m, and your best is kept.

Run GopherDig.exe. No installation needed (SDL2 is built in).

Controls                  Gamepad (SNES layout)      Keyboard
  walk (push on a step:     Left / Right               arrow keys
    climb it)
  drill where it faces      A (hold: again)            X
  drill down                Down + A                   Down + X
  start                     A (or Start, Down)         X or Enter
  pause / resume            Select (or Start in a run) Backspace or Esc
  players 2-4 join          A on their pad, on the title (B leaves)
  back to the title         A (or Select) on the results
  touch / mouse             tap the block beside or under the gopher to
                            drill it (hold: again); tap left or right of
                            it to walk there; a tap starts

Up to four gophers (yellow, blue and two more hats) race down the same well
at once, each in their own view and with their own pad. Each is out on their
own, the game ends when all are out, and the results rank everyone by depth,
with medals.

F11 or Alt+Enter: fullscreen. F12: screenshot. Close the window to quit.
Options: GopherDig.exe --scale 4 --fullscreen
The best depth is saved in gopherdig.srm next to the exe.
